**LAS VEGAS, Nevada (CNN)** -- Disgraced music mogul Julian "J-Vance" Vance appeared in a packed Clark County courtroom Thursday, where a Nevada judge ordered him held without bail on charges stemming from an alleged armed confrontation at a Las Vegas strip hotel last week.

`[Watch Vance enter the courtroom in handcuffs »]`

Vance, 42, wearing a yellow Nevada Department of Corrections jumpsuit and wrist restraints, spoke only briefly during the 15-minute arraignment, answering "Yes, your honor" when asked if he understood the eight felony counts against him, which include armed robbery, assault with a deadly weapon, and first-degree kidnapping.

Defense attorney Marcus Sterling urged Clark County District Judge Michelle Torrence to set bail at $100,000, arguing that Vance is a well-known public figure with deep business ties in California and Nevada.

"Mr. Vance is not a flight risk, nor is he a threat to the community," Sterling told the court. "This entire incident stems from a heated misunderstanding regarding stolen personal property that belonged to my client's late father. No shots were fired, and no one suffered serious physical injury."

However, Deputy District Attorney Sarah Lin pushed for remanded custody, presenting evidence that Vance purchased a one-way ticket to Paris shortly after police began questioning witnesses on Sunday morning.

"The defendant used armed muscle to enforce his own brand of justice in a private penthouse suite," Lin said. "He then immediately took steps to flee the jurisdiction. The state views Mr. Vance as a severe flight risk."

Judge Torrence sided with the prosecution, ordering Vance to remain in the Clark County Detention Center pending his next court appearance.

`[Watch prosecutor outline charges against Vance »]`

According to police reports, Vance and three unidentified associates entered a high-roller suite at the Grand Lux Resort & Casino shortly past midnight on October 19. Investigators allege Vance held two men at gunpoint while demanding the return of vintage studio equipment and jewelry valued at over $450,000. 

Authorities say a security camera captured Vance leaving the property carrying two large aluminum duffel bags. 

`[SEE ALSO: How Las Vegas casino security tracked the suspects »]`

If convicted on all charges, Vance faces a maximum sentence of 30 years to life in state prison under Nevada's strict armed robbery statutes.

A preliminary hearing has been scheduled for November 14. Outside the courtroom, Sterling told reporters his team plans to file an immediate appeal regarding the bail decision. 

"Julian looks forward to clearing his name," Sterling said. "When the facts come out, it will be clear that he was the victim of a scam, not the perpetrator of a crime."
